items.title: Brent hits 4-month high above $108 on Hormuz attack, Saudi pipeline shutdown
items.text: Brent crude touched $108/bbl intraday on 14 September, its highest in four months, before settling near $107.22 (+1.27%); WTI rose to $102.66 (+1.52%). The move followed an attack on a merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West pipeline after drone strikes, removing an alternate export route that had let crude bypass the chokepoint. Sustained high crude lifts realisations for India's upstream producers but adds to the country's import bill and inflation risk.

items.title: IEA cuts 2026 oil demand forecast as Gulf supply stays constrained
items.text: The IEA's September Oil Market Report cut its 2026 global oil demand forecast by a further 940,000 b/d to a decline of 2.5 mb/d for the year, while global supply fell 1.6 mb/d to 100.1 mb/d in August with more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output still shut in. Global observed inventories fell a steep 95 mb in August (2.8 mb/d), underscoring how tight the physical market remains even as demand softens - a dynamic that keeps Brent elevated and supportive for Indian upstream earnings.

items.title: ONGC, Oil India shares jump as Brent tops $100 on Hormuz crisis
items.text: ONGC gained nearly 2% and Oil India advanced about 2.4% on 10 September as Brent crude crossed $100/bbl (trading near $101.10) and WTI traded near $96.24, on escalating US-Iran tensions over the Middle East. Higher crude directly lifts realisations and profitability for India's state-run upstream producers.

items.title: OMC marketing margins turn deeply negative as Brent crosses $100
items.text: Indian oil marketing companies are estimated to be losing about Rs 5 per litre on petrol and Rs 23 per litre on diesel after Brent crude crossed $100/bbl, up sharply from the $70-75 range before the Iran conflict, while retail pump prices have stayed frozen since April 2022. Continued crude strength without a retail price revision squeezes marketing margins for IOC, BPCL and HPCL, even as refining margins provide some offsetting cushion.

items.title: HSBC, Goldman Sachs lift Brent forecasts as Indian basket hits $115.98
items.text: India's crude basket hit $115.98/bbl on 9 September, pushing the September-to-date average to $104.09 (+15.4% versus August's $90.19). HSBC raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $90/bbl from $80, citing threats to Hormuz shipping, while Goldman Sachs sees Brent averaging $85 in December 2026 and $80 in 2027, with a risk scenario above $120 if attacks on shipping intensify. Higher-for-longer crude supports realisations for ONGC, Oil India and other Indian producers but raises the import bill.
